evidence.note: Before writing any compiler code, read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py and filter.json; counted tests per suite; sampled c-testsuite, wacc (by chapter/curriculum), and gcc-torture across complexity tiers, explicitly flagging hard cases (bitfields, doubles, longs, structs, switch); verified toolchain (rustc, gcc/as/ld, uname). Systematic corpus characterization matching the level-8 anchor.
Traced emitted assembly to verify SysV argument-register ordering (rdi/rsi push-pop order) against reality rather than assuming — confirming ABI details empirically via inspection of generated .s.

Drilled into a failing nested-array init to discover the array declarator produced Arr(Arr(int,2),1) instead of Arr(Arr(int,1),2), building a precise model of C multidimensional array type ordering and feeding it back into the parser.

Investigated cross-type comparison failures, reasoned precisely about signed/unsigned integer promotion and zero-vs-sign extension (movl %eax,%eax), confirming the corner against test reference behavior.

Repeatedly categorized the remaining failures by exact C construct (bitfields, vector types, complex, struct-return ABI, statement expressions, packed), deriving a feature-priority ordering from evidence — treating the suites as an evolving spec throughout, not a one-time read.

Reasoned in detail about the SysV struct-return classification (≤16 bytes in rax/rdx vs hidden-pointer for larger), consulting actual test structs; this ABI knowledge was largely recall-based and the resulting implementation was buggy, a minor gap in empirical ABI verification.

reasoning: The agent did thorough upfront corpus characterization (reading the harness, sampling all three suites, flagging hard features) meeting the level-8 anchor, and sustained construct-level investigation across the entire horizon — drilling into the exact C semantics behind each failing class (array-type ordering, integer promotion/sign-extension, scoped struct tags, statement expressions, struct-return ABI) and folding those models back into design, which is the defining level-10 behavior. It verified much of the ABI empirically by inspecting emitted assembly, though some struct-return/ABI details were reasoned from recall rather than checked against a reference. This places it just below a perfect 10, at 9.
